proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the right of an owner to consume, destroy, or alienate a thing. In Roman law property theory it names one of the canonical sticks in the bundle of ownership rights (alongside usus and fructus). Like all legal rights in our ontology, it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a legal person and is externally grounded in the legal system that confers it; BFO_0000023 (Role) is therefore the appropriate type. It is a class (a kind of right), not an individual instance. It is best placed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class, which itself is already typed as BFO_0000023.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight: it is the specific right-component of ownership that authorises disposal or destruction of the res. Placing it as a subclass of LegalRight captures both its BFO typing (Role / specifically dependent continuant) and its domain position within property-law theory.

open_questions: Should we also model the complementary rights Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right of fruits) as sibling subclasses of LegalRight to complete the Roman dominium triad?

Should Abusus be treated as a class only, or do we also want a named individual representing, e.g., the Abusus right as instantiated in a specific Roman-law jurisdiction (e.g., classical Roman law, Justinianic law)?
Do we need a superclass 'OwnershipRight' or 'DominionComponent' intermediate between LegalRight and Abusus to group the bundle-of-rights components?
Should Abusus bear an additional BFO_0000016 (Disposition) facet capturing the capacity to alienate, or is the Role typing sufficient for current modelling purposes?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus in Roman property theory is the right of an owner to abuse—consume, destroy, or transfer—a thing (res). Ontologically, it is an externally grounded, specifically dependent continuant: it does not exist independently but inheres in whoever holds the legal status of dominus under a legal system that recognises it. This profile fits BFO_0000023 (Role) precisely, and it is already consonant with the existing working:LegalRight class (itself typed as BFO_0000023). Abusus is a kind of legal right, so it is modelled as a class (a natural kind in the domain of Roman property law) rather than an individual. It is introduced as a new class working:Abusus with rdfs:subClassOf working:LegalRight, inheriting the Role / specifically-dependent-continuant typing from its parent. No further BFO primitives are needed at this stage, though open questions flag whether the sibling rights Usus and Fructus, and an intermediate OwnershipRight grouping class, should also be minted.
